_transcription: PAGE MAP — the booklet is 12 rendered pages (idx 0..11 = printed folios 1..12) and EVERY page is accounted for. idx 0 = bilingual cover (Series AABB3/1, SET-1, Q.P. Code 56/1/1, 'CHEMISTRY (Theory)', Time 2 hours, Maximum Marks 35, '12 printed pages'). ENGLISH = the EVEN indices 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 (folios 3, 5, 7, 9, 11). HINDI = the ODD indices 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 (folios 2, 4, 6, 8, 10). idx 11 (folio 12) is BLANK — only a rule, an asterisk and the footer. The alternating hypothesis held exactly, with NO parity inversion. I checked the TOP ~22% of all five odd indices in one montage: every one opens in Hindi (idx 1 Hindi General Instructions, idx 3 Hindi Q3, idx 5 Hindi Q6, idx 7 Hindi Q10, idx 9 Hindi Q12-continuation) — there is NO English overflow onto any odd top. ⚠ THE CONTACT SHEET LIES ABOUT idx 11: at thumbnail size it shows what looks like English content (a benzene-ring reaction block and 'Write the major products of the following reactions'). That is scanner show-through from the reverse of the sheet, i.e. the ghost of folio 11. Confirmed BLANK at full size — exactly the failure mode the brief warns about for 2022 65/5/3. English content flows continuously Q1 -> Q12 across the five English pages: idx 2 = instructions + Section A + Q1, Q2; idx 4 = Q3 + Section B header + Q4, Q5(a)/(b); idx 6 = Q6, Q7(a)/(b), Q8(a)/(b), Q9; idx 8 = Q10(a)/(b), Q11, Section C header + Q12 passage paragraphs 1-2; idx 10 = Q12 passage paragraph 3 + sub-parts (a)-(d) + the (d) OR branch. Q12 is the only question split across a page boundary. STRUCTURE read off the paper's own printed English General Instructions on idx 2 and it matches `term2_sci` EXACTLY: (i) 12 questions, all compulsory; (ii) three Sections A, B, C; (iii) Section A Q1-3 very short answer, 2 marks each; (iv) Section B Q4-11 short answer, 3 marks each; (v) Section C Q12 case based, 5 marks; (vi) log tables and calculators NOT allowed. 6 + 24 + 5 = 35, matching the cover's Maximum Marks 35 and the marking scheme's 'A full scale of marks 0-35 has to be used'. ⚠ DISAGREEMENT: there are only SIX printed instructions and NONE of them mentions internal choice — unlike the Maths 2022 term2 paper, whose instruction (vi) announces it. So the paper announces no count and the marking scheme is the only authority. I walked the scheme question by question: it reprints an explicit OR block for Q5, Q7, Q8, Q10 and for sub-part Q12(d), and for NO other question. That is 5 internal choices, all ingested as paired rows. Q11 prints (a) and (b) with NO 'OR' between them and a combined '2 + 1 = 3' — the scheme confirms it by giving both parts under one '11.' row with no OR — so Q11 is ONE question with two sub-parts, not a choice. ⚠ DECIMAL POINTS: this paper prints ORDINARY BASELINE full stops ('0.3010', '76.3'), NOT the raised dots the 2023 paper and the brief describe. Verified at 2x zoom on both occurrences. So no `{\cdot}` is used for decimals anywhere here. The one middle dot that IS printed is the abbreviation separator in 'Conc . NaOH' on idx 10, which is transcribed as \cdot inside the reaction arrow. NO MCQs at all, so there is no Section-A key table in the marking scheme, no `answer` field on any row and nothing for `audit:keys` to scan. NO question was voided by CBSE — I read all five scheme answer pages (ms/p01..p05) and there is no 'full mark to be awarded' / 'printing error' note anywhere. CHAPTERS: Q10 (both branches) is Surface Chemistry, dropped by NCERT's rationalisation, and is filed on `Surface Chemistry [Outdated]`; every other question maps to one of the ten live chapters. Nothing is out of syllabus. 20 rows for 12 questions (12 primaries + 5 OR-alternatives + the 3 extra case-study sub-parts).

questions.stem: Define rate of reaction. Write two factors that affect the rate of reaction.

Arrange the following compounds as directed : (any Two)
(i) In decreasing order of basic strength in aqueous solution :
\(\mathrm{C_2H_5NH_2}\), \(\mathrm{(C_2H_5)_2NH}\), \(\mathrm{(C_2H_5)_3N}\)
(ii) In increasing order of solubility in water :
\(\mathrm{(C_2H_5)_2NH}\), \(\mathrm{C_2H_5NH_2}\), \(\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2}\)
(iii) In decreasing order of their pKb values :
\(\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2}\), \(\mathrm{C_2H_5NH_2}\), \(\mathrm{NH_3}\)

Write the Nernst equation for the following cell reaction :
\(\mathrm{Zn(s)} + \mathrm{Cu^{2+}\,(aq)} \rightarrow \mathrm{Zn^{2+}\,(aq)} + \mathrm{Cu(s)}\)
How will the \(\mathrm{E_{cell}}\) be affected when concentration of
(i) \(\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}\) ions is increased and
(ii) \(\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}\) ions is increased ?

questions.stem:
Following ions of 3d-transition series are given :
\(\mathrm{Ti^{4+}}\), \(\mathrm{V^{3+}}\), \(\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}\), \(\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}\)
(Atomic number : Ti = 22, V = 23, Cr = 24, Mn = 25)
Identify the ion which is
(i) most stable in aqueous solution.
(ii) a strong oxidising agent.
(iii) colourless in aqueous solution.
Give suitable reason in each.

(i) On the basis of crystal field theory, write the electronic configuration for \(\mathrm{d^4}\) ion if \(\Delta_0 < \mathrm{P}\).
(ii) Using valence bond theory, predict the hybridization and magnetic character of \(\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}\).
(Atomic number of Ni = 28)
(iii) Write the formula of the following complex using IUPAC norms :
Dichloridobis (ethane-1,2-diamine) cobalt (III)

When a co-ordination compound \(\mathrm{NiCl_2 \cdot 6H_2O}\) mixed with \(\mathrm{AgNO_3}\), 2 moles of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\) are precipitated per mole of the compound. Write
(i) Structural formula of the complex.
(ii) Secondary valency of 'Ni' in the complex.
(iii) IUPAC name of the complex.

A first order reaction is 50% complete in 40 minutes. Calculate the time required for the completion of 90% of reaction.
[Given : log 2 = 0.3010, log 10 = 1]

Illustrate the following reactions giving suitable example in each case :
(i) Gabriel phthalimide synthesis.
(ii) Carbylamine reaction.
(iii) Hoffmann bromamide degradation reaction.

Write the structures of A, B and C in the following reactions :
(i) \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2Cl} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{KCN}} \mathrm{A} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{LiAlH_4}} \mathrm{B} \xrightarrow[0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}]{\mathrm{HNO_2}} \mathrm{C}\)
(ii) \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH} \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\mathrm{NH_3}} \mathrm{A} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{(b)\ H_2O}]{\mathrm{(a)\ LiAlH_4}} \mathrm{B} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{C_6H_5SO_2Cl}} \mathrm{C}\)

questions.stem:
An organic compound 'X' with the molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_5H_{10}O}\) forms 2,4-DNP derivative, does not reduce Tollens' reagent but gives positive iodoform test on heating with \(\mathrm{I_2}\) in the presence of NaOH. Compound 'X' gives ethanoic acid and propanoic acid on vigorous oxidation. Write the
(i) Structure of the compound 'X'.
(ii) Structure of the product obtained when compound 'X' reacts with 2,4-DNP reagent.
(iii) Structures of the products obtained when compound 'X' is heated with \(\mathrm{I_2}\) in the presence of NaOH.
Write any three differences between physisorption and chemisorption.

Define the following terms with a suitable example in each :
(i) Lyophilic sol
(ii) Macromolecular colloid
(iii) Coagulation

questions._flag: Two printed-notation defects, transcribed as printed. (1) The Faraday constant is given as '1F = 96500 mol^-1' — the coulomb is missing from the unit; it should be 96500 C mol^-1, as the marking scheme itself writes. (2) Part (b) asks for lowercase lambda-nought-m for MgCl2, i.e. the symbol for a single ION's limiting molar conductivity, where the electrolyte's limiting molar conductivity (capital Lambda-nought-m) is meant; the marking scheme answers with capital Lambda. Neither defect changes what is being asked.

(a) The standard Gibbs energy \((\Delta_{\mathrm{r}}\mathrm{G}^{\circ})\) for the following cell reaction is \(-300\) kJ \(\mathrm{mol^{-1}}\) :
\(\mathrm{Zn(s)} + 2\mathrm{Ag^{+}(aq)} \rightarrow \mathrm{Zn^{2+}\,(aq)} + 2\mathrm{Ag(s)}\)
Calculate \(\mathrm{E^{o}_{cell}}\) for the reaction. (Given: 1F = 96500 \(\mathrm{mol^{-1}}\))
(b) Calculate \(\lambda^{o}_{m}\) for \(\mathrm{MgCl_2}\) if \(\lambda^{o}\) values for \(\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}\) ion and \(\mathrm{Cl^{-}}\) ion are 106 S \(\mathrm{cm^2mol^{-1}}\) and 76.3 S \(\mathrm{cm^2mol^{-1}}\) respectively.

questions.subtopic: Chemical Reactions of Aldehydes and Ketones
questions.context:
Aldehydes, ketones and carboxylic acids are some of the important classes of organic compounds containing carbonyl group. These are highly polar molecules due to higher electro-negativity of oxygen relative to carbon in the carbonyl group. Aldehydes are prepared by dehydrogenation or controlled oxidation of primary alcohols and controlled reduction of acyl halides. Ketones are prepared by oxidation of secondary alcohols and hydration of alkynes.
Aldehydes and ketones undergo nucleophilic addition reactions onto the carbonyl group but carboxylic acid does not undergo nucleophilic addition reaction. The alpha \((\alpha)\) – hydrogens of aldehydes and ketones are acidic. Therefore aldehydes and ketones having at least one \(\alpha\)-hydrogen undergo Aldol condensation.
Aldehydes are easily oxidised by mild oxidising agents such as Tollens' reagent and Fehling's reagent. Carboxylic acids are prepared by the oxidation of primary alcohols, aldehydes and by hydrolysis of nitriles. Aromatic carboxylic acids are prepared by side-chain oxidation of alkyl benzenes. Carboxylic acids are considerably more acidic than alcohols and most of simple phenols.
questions.stem:
